primary_reviews.rationale: The resumptive וַיְהִי בְּ + infinitive-construct formula opening 2:8 is a legitimate, independently sufficient scene-reopening marker after the 2:5-7 genealogical digression, and the subsequent content (Esther's concealment notice, Mordecai's daily vigil) is correctly bounded before the ritual-procedure description opens at 2:12. This also matches the book strategy's own dat sweep member list, which places this chapter's first genuine dat occurrence at 2:8 (then 2:12), with nothing in 2:1-2:4. The row's parenthetical gloss ('the king' and 'his decree') does not correspond to what וְיַפְקֵ֨ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ actually says. This is a lexical/count-object-adjacent error -- conflating two distinct Hebrew roots under one 'decree' label -- though it does not collapse the boundary argument, since the case for opening a new unit at 2:8 stands independently of this flawed etymological aside.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation: every Hebrew string in this row was collated with collate.py against its asserted oshb: ref; all returned tier=byte (quotation-grade). Both quotes byte: the Esth.9.1 fronted date string (including the resumptive pronoun) and the reversal clause. The two load-bearing numbers verify: the reversal spelling returns 1 verse (Esth.9.1) and the nifal at Esth.9.22 is a genuinely distinct string returning 1 verse, so counting them separately is correct; the fear-fell formula returns 3 verses (Esth.8.17, 9.2, 9.3), matching the row. The seam itself I judge well argued from the closer's side and independently sound: Esth.9.1 is a verbless-headed temporal frame with no wayyiqtol until the next verse, and the reversal clause is the chapter thesis. The defect is the one formal parallel the row adduces to corroborate the superscription. It asserts a month-then-day fronting shared with two named earlier notices; neither notice has the shape claimed. Because the claim is repeated in the substrate signals as a standing form argument, and because it is the only formal support offered beyond the row's own verse, it is worth contesting even though the verdict on the span would not change.

challenges.claim: The asserted 'same month-then-day fronting used to open the pur-casting notice and the edict-drafting notice' holds at neither verse: the pur-casting notice fronts month-then-YEAR with no day element, and the edict-drafting notice's date is post-verbal, so it opens nothing.
challenges.evidence: Pur-casting notice, byte-collated slice: בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ הוּא חֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֔ן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה (oshb:Esth.3.7) — month, appositional month-name, then a regnal YEAR; the day element the row's pattern requires is absent, and the only day language in that verse is the distributive day-to-day phrase later in the clause. Edict-drafting notice, byte-collated slice: וַיִּקָּרְאוּ֩ סֹפְרֵ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֣ר יוֹם֮ בּוֹ֒ (oshb:Esth.3.12) — the date does carry month-then-day, but it is post-verbal: the verse opens with the scribes-summons wayyiqtol, so the date does not 'open' the verse and cannot be a fronting parallel. Swept rather than asserted: the appositional month-naming formula on which the row's claimed pattern depends returns 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 book-wide — Esth.2.16, 3.7, 3.13, 8.9, 8.12, 9.1); of those, 3 are verse-initial date frames (Esth.3.7, 8.12, 9.1), and of those 3 the month-then-day order holds at 1 (sweep: 1 book-wide), namely Esth.9.1 itself — Esth.3.7 is month-then-year as shown, and Esth.8.12 inverts to day-then-month, “on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar” (web:Esth.8.12). The other 3 members (Esth.2.16, 3.13, 8.9) are all post-verbal, Esth.8.9 behind the same scribes-summons verb as Esth.3.12. Consequence: the claim is not merely unswept (no digit is attached to it anywhere in the row) but false as stated, and neither supporting verse appears in boundary_evidence_refs, so the assertion is unverifiable from the row's own citation set. The row's primary warrants — the fronted date frame and the reversal clause, sweep: 1 book-wide for that spelling, re-derived — stand unaffected.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation: every Hebrew string in this row was collated with collate.py against its asserted oshb: ref; all returned tier=byte (quotation-grade). Five quotes, all byte. The span is defensible: Esth.9.2 resumes mainline narration after the Esth.9.1 frame, and Esth.9.6 opens with a fronted locative that genuinely narrows scope, so a break at Esth.9.5|9.6 is well motivated. My objections are to the row's grammar and to its evidence handling, not to the seam. The rejected_alternative rests on a syntactic claim about Esth.9.3-9.4 that the pointed text does not support: Esth.9.4 is indeed a causal clause throughout, but Esth.9.3 is a waw-plus-fronted-compound-subject participial clause whose predicate is finite in force, with only its final clause causal. That matters because the rejected rival is dismissed precisely on the ground that neither verse carries a mainline verb. Separately, three of the five quote/gloss pairs do not cover the same span, twice in ways that leave load-bearing material untranslated. The interior mark is disclosed but its direction is presented backwards relative to the rival the row rejects.

challenges.claim: Syntax mislabel: the row calls Esth.9.3 and Esth.9.4 'two causal clauses' that 'stay grammatically subordinate', but Esth.9.3 is an independent waw-clause with a fronted compound subject and a participial predicate; only its final clause is causal.
challenges.evidence: Byte-collated slice of the relevant stretch of Esth.9.3: וְכָל שָׂרֵ֨י הַמְּדִינ֜וֹת וְהָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִ֣ים וְהַפַּח֗וֹת וְעֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מְנַשְּׂאִ֖ים אֶת הַיְּהוּדִ֑ים (oshb:Esth.9.3) — waw plus a four-member compound NP subject, a relative qualifier, then the participial predicate governing the definite object; WEB renders it as a full independent sentence, “All the princes of the provinces, the local governors, the governors, and those who did the king's business helped the Jews” (web:Esth.9.3). The causal element begins only after that, and the row's own quote of Esth.9.3 starts inside the object NP rather than at the causal particle. By contrast Esth.9.4 is causal from its first word, as the row's byte-true quote of it shows. The rejected_alternative's stated warrant — 'neither carries a mainline verb and both stay grammatically subordinate' — is therefore false for one of the two verses, which weakens (it does not refute) the case against splitting Esth.9.3-9.4 off. Note the row's own unit_type, 'narrative summary with causal aside', is singular where the rationale is plural, so the internal description is also inconsistent.

challenges.claim: Three quote/gloss pairs cover different spans: at Esth.9.2 and Esth.9.5 a full-verse Hebrew quote is paired with a part-verse WEB gloss, and at Esth.9.3 the Hebrew begins and ends outside the glossed clause.
challenges.evidence: Esth.9.2: the Hebrew quote runs to the end of the verse, but the paired gloss stops at “to lay hands on those who wanted to harm them” (web:Esth.9.2), leaving the byte-collated tail וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא עָמַ֣ד לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי נָפַ֥ל פַּחְדָּ֖ם עַל כָּל הָעַמִּֽים (oshb:Esth.9.2) untranslated — and that tail is the very fear-fell clause the neighbouring Esth.9.1 unit adduces as cross-seam evidence. Esth.9.5: the Hebrew quote runs to the end of the verse, but the gloss stops at “The Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword” (web:Esth.9.5), leaving מַכַּת חֶ֥רֶב וְהֶ֖רֶג וְאַבְדָ֑ן וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְשֹׂנְאֵיהֶ֖ם כִּרְצוֹנָֽם (oshb:Esth.9.5) untranslated — this is the clause the row characterises as the general summary of the day's violence, so it is load-bearing. Esth.9.3: the Hebrew quote opens at the definite object of the preceding participial predicate (glossed nowhere) and stops before the prepositional phrase that the paired gloss “because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them” (web:Esth.9.3) does render — that phrase is the byte-collated עֲלֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Esth.9.3), which sits outside the quote. All three are span-sync failures in the sense the standing rule names; none is a fidelity failure (check_web_quotes returned 0 flags, so the English is verbatim as far as it goes).

challenges.claim: The row calls the verb opening 9:2 a wayyiqtol and calls 9:5's verb 'a second resumptive wayyiqtol,' but 9:2's verb carries no vav-consecutive prefix and is not a wayyiqtol at all.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Esth.9.2 opens with נִקְהֲל֨וּ -- a bare Niphal perfect (no vav-consecutive prefix). Contrast oshb:Esth.9.5, which opens וַיַּכּ֤וּ, a true wayyiqtol (וַ + prefix-conjugation), and oshb:Esth.9.15, which uses the SAME root as 9:2 but WITH the consecutive prefix: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ. primary_reviews.rationale: Re-derived rather than trusted. The 9:22|23 seam (hazard region 8) is genuinely two-sided: 9:20-22 is one Hebrew sentence governed by Mordecai's finite verbs (vayikhtov/vayishlach, 9:20) with 9:21-22 as subordinate infinitival/relative continuations of what he wrote, closing grammatically at the end of 9:22; 9:23 opens a new sentence with a new grammatical subject (hayehudim) and a new main verb (veqibel). The row's framing -- 9:22 is 'the letter's own instructions' vs 9:23 opens reception -- correctly names both sides of that seam rather than only the opening side, and it honestly discloses the residual weakness (no explicit new-document formula at 9:23) rather than overclaiming; confidence medium is calibrated to that. Span 9:23-28 matches the confirmation-block default unit named in the strategy's inset rule, and the row does not sever it. The ki(9:24)...al ken(9:26) causal-resultative reading behind the rejected_alternative is grammatically sound (9:24 opens with the causal ki, 9:26 resumes with the resumptive al ken) -- verified against the actual clause structure, not assumed. challenges.claim: The row contrasts 9:31's fasting noun with “the finite tsom forms used for the original fast at 4:3 and 4:16”, but 4:3 is a noun in a coordinated noun series, and 9:31's form is the plural of that same noun — the finiteness contrast does not exist, and the singular “that spelling” covers two different spellings.
challenges.evidence: 4:3 reads אֵ֤בֶל גָּדוֹל֙ לַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְצ֥וֹם — the fasting word stands coordinated with the nouns for mourning, weeping and wailing, and WEB renders the series “there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing” (web:Esth.4.3). Within the pair the row names, the finite forms stand at 4:16 — 2 tokens: וְצ֣וּמוּ עָ֠לַי (imperative) and וְנַעֲרֹתַ֖י אָצ֣וּם (1cs yiqtol) — while 4:3 carries the noun. The 9:31 form דִּבְרֵ֥י הַצֹּמ֖וֹת וְזַעֲקָתָֽם (collate tier byte) is the definite plural of the 4:3 noun; consonantal sweep for the plene string: 2 book-wide (4:3, 4:16) — the digit is right — and consonantal sweep for the 9:31 defective plural string: 1 book-wide (9:31).
